pairs.why: They are almost the same cup, but B has a little foam on the tea and slightly deeper shading, which gives it a bit more of the lived-in detail the real juice glass has; A is plainer.
A has bubbles on the tea, a richer amber color and a fuller, more solid cup, so it is closer to the vivid finish of the real cards; B is a little flat and bare.
Both cups have the same build, gloss and color, and the only differences are tiny steam and foam changes that do not move either one closer to the real cards.
A has a light foam edge, slightly stronger contrast and a more solid cup body, while B looks a bit plainer and softer next to the punchy real cards.
B has more saturated tea with small bubbles and slightly deeper shading at the edges, so it reads livelier, like the real juice glass; A is the plainer version.
A has richer orange tea with bubbles, clearer steam and stronger form shading, which matches the vivid, slightly glossy real cards better than the plainer B.
A's foamy surface and fuller, brighter tea give it more of the real cards' small believable detail, while B is nearly bare.
B has a visible ring of bubbles and slightly crisper rim shading, so it looks a little more like a real, vivid object from the game; A is marginally flatter.
